title: Early Career Rotational Program - hiring plan & 90-day onboarding checklist
content:
Purpose
This doc captures a working hiring plan and a pragmatic 90-day onboarding checklist for the Early Career Rotational Program (ECRP). Aim: hire 6 rotating contributors (new grads + junior hires) across Eng infra, Serving Runtime, and Product over Q1–Q2 2026. Focus on fast ramp, measurable learning outcomes, and cross-team visibility.

Goals and success metrics
- Hire 6 people: 2 infra, 2 serving-runtime, 2 product/console. Target diversity mix + at least 50% first-time hires moving from college or bootcamps.
- Time-to-productivity: contributors should complete first independent PR in 30 days and lead a small feature or bug fix in 90 days.
- Retention: 80% conversion to full-time offers after successful rotations.
- Learning outcomes: each hire completes 3 rotation-specific learning milestones and one cross-team demo.

High-level timeline (draft)
- Nov 2025: finalize role specs, interview rubric, and panel leads
- Dec 2025: open roles on jobs site and campus channels; coordinate internship/grad office outreach
- Jan–Feb 2026: first round interviews (coding + behavioral + culture fit)
- Mar 2026: offers issued; pre-boarding materials sent
- Apr 2026: cohort start; 2-week onboarding sprint; rotations begin after week 3

Open questions (notes to self)
- Should rotations be 3 months or 4 months? Pros/cons: 3mo faster exposure; 4mo deeper project ownership. Recommendation: default 3 months + optional 4th-month extension for complex projects.
- Budget: confirm hiring budgets with finance for conversion bonuses and relocation stipends.

Role profiles (summary)
- Rotational Software Engineer - Serving Runtime: basic C++/Rust familiarity preferred, interest in inference kernels, debugging, and perf investigations.
- Rotational Software Engineer - Infrastructure: Linux, container systems, infra automation, basic Python and SRE concepts.
- Rotational Product Engineer - Console & Tooling: frontend fundamentals, API ergonomics, and product-focused design sense.

Interview framework and rubric (single-page summary)
Scoring: 1–4 scale mapped to pass/fail thresholds. Include calibration notes for panels.
- Technical fundamentals (coding, problem solving): 40%. Look for clarity of thought, correctness, and incremental approach.
- System thinking / architecture appropriate to level: 20%. For junior roles emphasize conceptual understanding more than scale.
- Behavioral & collaboration: 20%. Teamwork examples, learning ability, feedback receptivity.
- Growth potential & culture add: 20%. Curiosity, ownership, alignment with developer-first mission.

Numeric rubric guidance (interviewer cheat-sheet)
- 4 = Exceeds expectations for an early-career candidate: writes correct solutions quickly, explains tradeoffs, shows strong curiosity and learning examples.
- 3 = Meets expectations: correct solution with minor gaps, reasonable explanations, good communication.
- 2 = Partial: incompletely solved, needed significant hints, but shows some potential and good debugging steps.
- 1 = Not yet: major gaps in core fundamentals or communication, would require strong remediation.

Sample interview flow (45–60 min)
- 5 min intro + role context
- 25–30 min coding problem or debugging exercise
- 10 min system question or architecture thought experiment (level-appropriate)
- 5–10 min behavioral + candidate questions
- Panel debrief immediately after; fill scorecard in 15 mins.

Panel composition and interviewer training
- Every panel: 2 engineers (one from host team, one cross-team), 1 hiring manager or tech lead, optional people-ops interviewer for behavioral calibration.
- Mandatory interviewer calibration session before campus weeks and before first round each hiring cycle.

Debrief and decision rules
- Fast decision target: 48 hours from final interview to offer/no-offer decision.
- Scorecard threshold: average >=3.0 and no dimension below 2.
- For borderline cases, conduct a short take-home or follow-up pairing session.

Offer and preboarding checklist (before start date)
- Offer packet with role, rotation plan, mentor assignment, expected deliverables per rotation.
- Send "what to expect" guide: reading list, dev environment setup instructions, Slack channels, and pre-boarding micro-tasks (hello world repo clone + run tests).
- Assign mentor and buddy; schedule 30-min intro coffee prior to start.

90-day onboarding checklist (practical items)
Preboarding (2 weeks before start):
- HR paperwork + benefits enrollment completed
- Dev laptop imaged and shipped
- Access requested (GitHub, Slack, Jira, infra sandboxes)
Week 0 (first 5 working days):
- Day 0 orientation (company mission, security, code of conduct)
- Team orientation: team goals, recent projects, and current sprint board
- Environment check: run test suite, open first dev branch and a tiny PR
- 1:1 with mentor and manager to set 30/60/90 goals
First 30 days:
- Complete two learning modules: codebase walkthrough and infra debugging lab
- Ship first small PR that touches CI/tests + pass review
- Weekly demos to host team; collect feedback
30–60 days:
- Take ownership of a small ticket or bug and drive it to completion
- Cross-rotation pairing session (shadow another team for half day)
- Midpoint feedback loop: formal 1:1 with manager + mentor; adjust goals
60–90 days:
- Lead a small feature or major bugfix independently with reviews
- Deliver rotation demo and learning report to rotation cohort
- Formal conversion discussion: readiness for full-time offer or next rotation

Mentor & manager responsibilities (quick list)
- Mentor: weekly pairing, justify incremental tasks, skills coaching, review learning list.
- Manager: career conversations, blockers removal, performance calibrations, conversion recommendation.

Conversion and rotation switch checklist
- Conversion decision rubric: impact in rotations, learning progress, cultural fit, peer feedback.
- If switching rotations: handoff doc, updated 30-day plan for new host team, checklist of outstanding PRs and tests, and a pairing week.

Onboarding artifacts we should produce (action items)
- Short "ECRP starter playbook" doc with step-by-step environment setup and 10 microtasks. (owner: Priya)
- Interviewer training slides + 3 calibration exercises (owner: Evan)
- Mentor playbook (owner: Lucas)
- Finance ask: conversion bonus and relocation cap proposal (owner: Maya)

Risks and mitigations
- Risk: slow ramp due to platform complexity. Mitigation: create targeted "first 30 days" lab that simulates common developer tasks with guided solutions.
- Risk: interview bandwidth. Mitigation: one panel per week during campus push + hiring coordinator buffer days.

Appendix: sample onboarding microtasks (for preboarding and week 1)
- Clone repo, run unit tests (expected to succeed locally)
- Write a tiny doc on a debugging session and share in #ecrp-intros
- Fix a trivial lint issue and get PR merged
- Shadow an oncall rotation pairing for 1 hour (infra cohort)

Unresolved decisions and next steps
- Finalize rotation length (3 vs 4 months) by Nov 30
- Confirm budget lines with Finance by Dec 10
- Run interviewer calibration dry-run Jan 5

Notes: this is a working draft; expect additional iteration after partner teams (serving-runtime and infra) review. Keep language simple for campus recruiters and share a 1-page public-friendly version for job postings.
